<r>2 Mac 6:18-20</r>

<h>Reading 1</h>

<r>2 Mac 6:18-20</r>
<n>18</n> Eleazar one of the chief of the scribes, a man advanced in years, and of a comely countenance, was pressed to open his mouth to eat swine's flesh.
<n>19</n> But he, choosing rather a most glorious death than a hateful life, went forward voluntarily to the torment.
<n>20</n> And considering in what manner he was come to it, patiently bearing, he determined not to do any unlawful things for the love of life.

<r>2 Mac 6:23-25</r>

<n>24</n> For it doth not become our age, said he, to dissemble: whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, at the age of fourscore and ten years, was gone over to the life of the heathens:

<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>A</c>bsólve, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuórum delícta populórum: ut a peccatórum néxibus, quæ pro nostra fragilitáte contráximus, tua benignitáte liberémur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio Ss. Crispini et Crispiniani Martyrum</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Isti sunt Sancti, qui pro Dei amóre minas hóminum contempsérunt: sancti Mártyres in regno cælórum exsúltant cum Angelis. O quam pretiósa est mors Sanctórum, qui assídue assístunt ante Dóminum, et ab ínvicem non sunt separáti!

<r>℣.</r> Mirábilis Deus.
<r>℟.</r> In sanctis suis.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui nos concédis sanctórum Mártyrum tuórum Crispíni et Crispiniáni natalítia cólere: da nobis in ætérna beatitúdine de eórum societáte gaudére.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.c69781446b:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we beseech thee, absolve thy people from their offences, that through thy bountiful goodness we may all be delivered from the bands of those sins, which by our frailty we have committed.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of Ss. Crispini et Crispiniani Martyrum</r>
<r>Ant.</r> These are the holy ones who for the love of Christ, recked nothing of the threats of men. In the kingdom of heaven the holy martyrs are filled with joy in the company of Angels. O how precious in the sight of the Lord was the death of these His saints who now stand day and night in His presence and are not divided the one from the other.

<r>℣.</r> Mirábilis Deus.
<r>℟.</r> In sanctis suis.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, who dost permit us to keep the birthday of thy holy Martyrs Crispíni et Crispiniáni, grant that we may enjoy their fellowship in everlasting happiness.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.3c7045545b:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 26th 2027, the 26th day of the Moon, was born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyr, Pope Evaristus, who dyed the Church of God with his blood under the Emperor Hadrian.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Rogatian the Priest and Felicissimus, who were crowned with a glorious martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus. Holy Cyprian writeth of them in his epistle unto the Confessors.
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, (in the persecution under the Emperor Decius,) the holy martyrs Lucian, Florius, and their Companions.
<h>A</h>t Narbonne, the holy Confessor Rusticus, Bishop (of that see,) who enlightened the times of the Emperors Valentinian and Leo.
<h>A</h>t Salerno, (in the seventh century,) holy Gaudiosus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Pavia, (in the year 1229,) holy Fulke, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>lso (at Policastro, in the sixth century,) the holy Sub-deacon Quadragesimus, who raised a dead man to life, (as is related by the blessed Pope Gregory.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
